name: Technical
description: Icons as technical drawings with a friendly finish. Two optical sizes like a typeface, a light stroke that does not chase the pixel grid, construction on 45° increments, closed shapes, and gaps wide enough to survive 16px.

character.purpose: Icons for a tool someone uses all day. They should be read, not noticed.
principles: An icon should not take your attention. Utilitarian, but never ugly or boring.
Closer to a technical drawing than an illustration: a diagram with a friendly finish.
Keep the natural proportions of real objects. A pencil stays tall and narrow, a banknote stays wide. Distorted proportions read as a toy.
Draw a recurring part the same way every time it appears. Consistency across the set beats cleverness in one icon.
Extend a line rather than clip it short, the way a monospace face does.
Cut a slash flat through a shape. Never imply depth or a shadow.
Every icon must still read when it is reduced to a filled silhouette.
Detail is a budget, not a bonus. If it disappears at 16px, it should not be drawn.
